=============================

42

---

(SurrealQL
  (Number
    (Int)))

    (Int)))

    (Number
      (Int))))

===========================================
javascript :: JavaScript function with args
===========================================

-- Same leaf `JavaScriptBlock` as above. The nested `{` inside a string is
-- the point of this case: the scanner must not end the block there.
function(123, 1d2h) {
	const number = 123;
	if (test("{")) {
		return number.toString();
	}
}

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (FunctionJs
    (FunctionName)
    (ArgumentList
      (Number
        (Int))
      (Duration
        (DurationPart)
        (DurationPart)))
    (JavaScriptBlock)))

========================================
javascript :: Simple JavaScript function
========================================

-- `JavaScriptBlock` is a leaf: the external scanner consumes the whole
-- `{ ... }` as one token, and `grammar.js` says why it cannot hand back
-- BraceOpen / JavaScriptContent / BraceClose separately.
function() {
	return 42;
}

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (FunctionJs
    (FunctionName)
    (ArgumentList)
    (JavaScriptBlock)))

=========================================================
operators :: A sign separated from its digits is a prefix
=========================================================

-- `-5` is one signed `Number` token; `- 5` is a prefix applied to `5`.
-- The engine answers -5 either way; joining the sign lexically is what
-- keeps the two readings out of the parser.
RETURN - 5

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (Comment)
  (ReturnStatement
    (Keyword)
    (PrefixExpression
      (Operator)
      (Number
        (Int)))))

======================================================
operators :: A sign joined to its digits is one Number
======================================================

RETURN -5

---

(SurrealQL
  (ReturnStatement
    (Keyword)
    (Number
      (Int))))

==========================================================================
operators :: Remainder on strings parses; the engine rejects it at runtime
==========================================================================

/* Well-formed, and not a valid program: the engine answers
   "Cannot perform remainder with 'string' and 'string'".
   Operand types are the type checker's job, not the grammar's. */
"8" % "3"

---

(SurrealQL
  (BlockComment)
  (BinaryExpression
    (String)
    (Operator)
    (String)))

===========================================================================
operators :: Prefix minus on array parses; the engine rejects it at runtime
===========================================================================

/* Well-formed, and not a valid program: the engine answers
   "Cannot negate the value 'array'".
   Operand types are the type checker's job, not the grammar's. */
-[1, 2, 3]

---

(SurrealQL
  (BlockComment)
  (PrefixExpression
    (Operator)
    (Array
      (Number
        (Int))
      (Number
        (Int))
      (Number
        (Int)))))

==================================================
operators :: Prefix minus binds tighter than power
==================================================

-- `(-a) ** 2`, as the engine reads it: with $a = 2, `-$a ** 2` is 4
-a ** 2

---

(SurrealQL
  (Comment)
  (BinaryExpression
    (PrefixExpression
      (Operator)
      (Ident))
    (Operator)
    (Number
      (Int))))
